thread:
Dana: saw a regression in canary — a tiny fraction of short RPCs got stuck behind long-lived streams during a traffic burst, p95 latency doubled.
Ravi: sounds like admission and retry interactions again. do we treat streaming and non-streaming requests differently in the gateway?
Marta: currently only global queue + global retry budget. streams just hold open connections and prevent fast RPCs from getting workers.
Theo: propose two complementary changes: 1) explicit conn-type header (`x-rw-conn-type: stream|rpc`) for SDKs; 2) a per-route admission token pool where tokens are consumed on admission (including retries) and only refilled on success. this prevents failing surges from replenishing budget.
Dana: how do we handle legacy clients that won't set the header?
Marta: heuristic fallback: if Transfer-Encoding: chunked and first-chunk-latency > 120ms -> mark streaming. otherwise treat as short rpc. conservative default to short.
Ravi: also add "stream_idle_reclaim_ms" to reclaim worker slots from inactive streams (no chunks for 150ms) and let short RPCs jump in. reclaim should be rate limited per tenant to avoid thrash.
Theo: hedging/soft-retries must be disabled for marked streams. otherwise we risk doubling worker use.
Dana: what should gateway return when per-route pool exhausted? 429 + Retry-After by default, but SDKs can opt-in to async enqueue (202).
Marta: instrumentation: surface `admission.tokens_remaining`, `stream_detected`, `idle_reclaims` per-request in traces. add dashboard and alert on reclaim_rate > 5/s.
Ravi: quick example config: `route: /v1/complete; admission: tokens:300; refill_on_success:true; stream_idle_reclaim_ms:150; opt_in_header:x-rw-conn-type`.
Dana: owners? Marta will spec gateway changes + RFC, Ravi will prototype token-bucket logic, Theo will update SDK and docs. I'll own canary plan.
